v.why: Adding a direct input-to-output skip where the edge was missing restores a path and helps more than replacing an existing conv/op on that edge.
When edge 3 already holds a strong 3x3 conv, the extra conv on edge 4 yields diminishing returns (+0.7 vs +2.2/+1.5 in experiments 1-3).
Replacing a weak avg_pool with a 3x3 conv gives a large gain on all datasets.
With edge 3 absent, edge 5 is a main route to the output, so removing it hurts more (C100 -4.68 vs -2.30).
When the other output edges are none, adding a skip on edge 3 reconnects input to output, giving a huge gain (experiment 10).
Replacing a missing first edge with a 3x3 conv gains more than upgrading an existing skip or pool.
Swapping a skip for a pool costs less than replacing a 1x1 conv with pooling (experiments 12-14).
Replacing the output skip with a conv is generally beneficial when the rest of the cell is conv-rich, and more so when edge 1 is not skip.
Adding a skip on the missing edge 2 helps IN16 more than replacing a conv1x1 does (experiments 4-6).
With edge 1 as skip, changing edge 5 to a 1x1 conv hurts on C10 and C100 (experiment 20) relative to a conv3x3 edge 1.
